title: Duke Energy gears up for Thanksgiving week storms, urges Carolinas customers to prepare for potential outages
summary: Duke Energy is preparing to respond to potential damage and power outages in the Carolinas caused by high winds and rain.
body_markdown:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. – Duke Energy is preparing to respond to potential damage and power outages in the Carolinas caused by high winds and rain.


**What to watch**


- Customers in the eastern half of the Carolinas face the biggest risk of power outages, especially those along the North Carolina coast and in the Triangle, due to rain and wind gusts.


- Duke Energy lineworkers and support teams are checking equipment and preparing materials needed to make repairs and restore power.


- Crews across the Carolinas are also preparing to move to the hardest-hit areas.


**Our view**


**Joe Huff, Duke Energy storm director:**


- “We’re monitoring conditions closely and getting our crews and equipment ready to respond as soon as it’s safe.”


- “Among our biggest concerns are the strong wind gusts expected in the eastern half of the Carolinas. They can bring down trees and power poles and slow restoration efforts.”


- “We encourage customers to prepare now, stay informed of the weather forecast and always avoid downed power lines.”


**What customers should do now**


- **Make a plan and prepare an emergency kit:** Charge phones, gather flashlights and extra batteries, and review other[critical actions](https://www.duke-energy.com/safety-and-preparedness/storm-safety/before-the-storm) .


- **Download or update the Duke Energy app:** Available on the Apple[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/duke-energy/id1325217974) and[Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.dukeenergy.customerapp.release) .


- **Confirm Duke Energy account login info:** Log in via[My Account](https://www.duke-energy.com/home/my-account?_gl=1*1e6rim2*_gcl_au*MTc3MjYxMzQzNC4xNzkxMzExMTQy*_ga*MjE2MDc3NDExLjE3OTEzMTExNDE.*_ga_HB58MJRNTY*czE3OTE1NTkzOTckbzckZzEkdDE3OTE1NjM1NzckajYwJGwwJGgw) or[mobile app](https://www.duke-energy.com/home/products/duke-energy-app?_gl=1*1e6rim2*_gcl_au*MTc3MjYxMzQzNC4xNzkxMzExMTQy*_ga*MjE2MDc3NDExLjE3OTEzMTExNDE.*_ga_HB58MJRNTY*czE3OTE1NTkzOTckbzckZzEkdDE3OTE1NjM1NzckajYwJGwwJGgw) to review and update contact info and communications preferences.


- **Sign up for outage alerts:** Receive[outage information](https://www.duke-energy.com/outages/alerts?_gl=1*1e6rim2*_gcl_au*MTc3MjYxMzQzNC4xNzkxMzExMTQy*_ga*MjE2MDc3NDExLjE3OTEzMTExNDE.*_ga_HB58MJRNTY*czE3OTE1NTkzOTckbzckZzEkdDE3OTE1NjM1NzckajYwJGwwJGgw) and restoration updates by text, phone or email.


- **Know how to report an outage:** Submit reports[online](https://outagereport.duke-energy.com/?_gl=1*1e6rim2*_gcl_au*MTc3MjYxMzQzNC4xNzkxMzExMTQy*_ga*MjE2MDc3NDExLjE3OTEzMTExNDE.*_ga_HB58MJRNTY*czE3OTE1NTkzOTckbzckZzEkdDE3OTE1NjM1NzckajYwJGwwJGgw) , via mobile app, by texting OUT to 57801 or by calling 800.POWERON (800.769.3766).


**What customers should expect**


- **Safety first:** Stay away from[downed power lines](https://www.duke-energy.com/safety-and-preparedness/storm-safety/safety-around-power-lines) and storm debris, and use[generators safely](https://www.duke-energy.com/outages/generators) .


- **Grid improvements help speed restoration:** Duke Energy has upgraded poles and wires, placed outage-prone lines underground and added smart,[self-healing technology](https://www.duke-energy.com/our-company/future/self-healing-technology) that can reroute power automatically – helping reduce the number and length of outages.


- **Outages still possible:** Severe weather can cause extended outages, even with these improvements in place.


- **Restoration takes time:** Crews will begin assessing damage and[restoring power](https://www.duke-energy.com/outages/restoring-your-power) as soon as it’s safe. In some areas, blocked roads, hidden damage or hazardous travel may delay restoration.


- **Crew safety:** Crews cannot work from bucket trucks when winds reach 30 mph or higher, which may slow restoration in some areas.

**Duke Energy**


Duke Energy (NYSE: DUK), a Fortune 150 company headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., is one of America’s largest energy holding companies. The company’s electric utilities serve 8.7 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, and collectively own 55,700 megawatts of energy capacity. Its natural gas utilities serve 1.6 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio and Kentucky.


Duke Energy is executing an energy modernization strategy, keeping customer value at the forefront as it invests in electric grid upgrades and efficient generation resources to strengthen the system and serve growing energy needs.


More information is available at[duke-energy.com](https://www.duke-energy.com/) . Follow Duke Energy on X, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook for stories about the people and innovations powering its communities.
